title: Build Horizon and the Builder Extended Rate Lock Loan Limit
content:
A long wait between the lock request and the home's estimated completion lowers the allowed loan-to-value percent used for a Builder Extended Rate Lock's resized loan limit.

**Rule.** The build horizon is the calendar days from the lock request date to the Home Purchase Agreement's estimated completion date. A horizon above 240 days takes 2.0 points off the allowed loan-to-value percent; a horizon above 180 days up to 240 days takes 1.0 point off; a shorter horizon takes nothing off. The points are taken from the allowed loan-to-value percent before it is applied to the price basis.

| Build horizon | Off the allowed loan-to-value percent |
|---|---|
| 180 days or fewer | nothing |
| 181 to 240 days | 1.0 point |
| 241 days or more | 2.0 points |

The request date is read from the lock record; the estimated completion date from the Home Purchase Agreement record of the agreement the lock finances.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical horizons)

| Horizon | Off |
|---|---|
| 180 | nothing |
| 181 | 1.0 |
| 240 | 1.0 |
| 241 | 2.0 |
